title: Newton's Second Law

variables.name: Net force
variables.description: Total force acting on an object.

variables.name: Acceleration
variables.description: Rate of change of velocity.

variables.name: Mass
variables.description: A measure of the object's inertia.

description: The acceleration of an object is proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to its mass.

idealizations.name: Friction
idealizations.note: Intro derivations usually assume idealized low-friction motion.

idealizations.name: Air resistance
idealizations.note: Drag is neglected to keep acceleration approximately constant.

title: Work-Energy Theorem

variables.name: Net work
variables.description: Total work done by all forces.

variables.name: Change in kinetic energy
variables.description: Difference between final and initial kinetic energy.

description: Net work on a body changes its kinetic energy, linking force-based motion to energy language.

idealizations.name: Friction
idealizations.note: Dissipative losses are often ignored in first-pass applications.

idealizations.name: Air resistance
idealizations.note: Drag work is omitted in idealized work-energy examples.

title: Conservation of Momentum

variables.name: Momentum
variables.description: Product of mass and velocity.

variables.name: System momentum sum
variables.description: Total momentum over all objects in the system.

description: For an isolated system, total momentum stays constant during interactions like collisions and explosions.

idealizations.name: External impulses
idealizations.note: The principle is introduced assuming negligible external force over collision time.

title: Kinematics (v = v0 + at)

variables.name: Acceleration
variables.description: Constant acceleration during motion.

variables.name: Time
variables.description: Elapsed time interval.

variables.name: Initial velocity
variables.description: Velocity at the start of motion.

variables.name: Final velocity
variables.description: Velocity after elapsed time.

description: This constant-acceleration relation predicts velocity changes over time without directly using forces.

idealizations.name: Friction
idealizations.note: Surface interactions are typically neglected in introductory kinematics.

title: Gravitational Potential Energy

variables.name: Mass
variables.description: Mass of the object.

variables.name: Gravitational field strength
variables.description: Acceleration due to gravity.

variables.name: Height
variables.description: Vertical displacement from a reference level.

variables.name: Potential energy
variables.description: Energy stored due to height in a gravitational field.

description: An object elevated in a gravitational field stores energy that can convert into kinetic energy.

idealizations.name: Local gravity variation
idealizations.note: Intro treatments assume constant g near Earth's surface.

title: Coulomb's Law

variables.name: Charges
variables.description: Point charges producing the interaction.

variables.name: Separation distance
variables.description: Distance between charge centers.

variables.name: Coulomb constant
variables.description: Proportionality constant in vacuum.

variables.name: Electrostatic force magnitude
variables.description: Force between two point charges.

description: The electric force between two point charges scales with charge product and falls with inverse-square distance.

idealizations.name: Material medium
idealizations.note: The vacuum form is emphasized before introducing dielectric effects.

title: Electric Field (F = qE)

variables.name: Electric field
variables.description: Force per unit positive test charge.

variables.name: Test charge
variables.description: Charge used to probe the field.

variables.name: Electric force
variables.description: Force experienced by a test charge.

description: Electric field describes how strongly and in what direction charges would be pushed at each point in space.

idealizations.name: Polarization effects
idealizations.note: Intro field definitions assume simple media or vacuum behavior.

title: Ohm's Law (I = V/R)

variables.name: Voltage
variables.description: Electrical potential difference across a component.

variables.name: Current
variables.description: Rate of charge flow.

variables.name: Resistance
variables.description: Opposition to current.

description: In many conductors, voltage is proportional to current with resistance as the proportionality constant.

idealizations.name: Temperature
idealizations.note: Resistance is treated as constant in the linear ohmic regime.

title: Faraday's Law of Induction

variables.name: Magnetic flux
variables.description: Magnetic field passing through an area.

variables.name: Time
variables.description: Time over which flux changes.

variables.name: Induced emf
variables.description: Voltage generated by changing magnetic flux.

description: A changing magnetic flux induces an emf, which drives current in a closed loop.

idealizations.name: Circuit resistance
idealizations.note: The flux-emf relation is introduced independent of resistive details.

title: Gauss's Law

variables.name: Enclosed charge
variables.description: Net charge inside the Gaussian surface.

variables.name: Vacuum permittivity
variables.description: Electric constant in free space.

variables.name: Area element
variables.description: Outward-oriented differential surface vector.

variables.name: Electric field
variables.description: Field passing through a closed surface.

description: Total electric flux through a closed surface equals enclosed charge divided by vacuum permittivity.

idealizations.name: Symmetry imperfections
idealizations.note: Canonical examples assume ideal geometric symmetry for tractable flux integrals.
